reviews.review: l4d if it's unfinished and boring

I bought this game when it came out and that was a massive mistake. It was absolutely not worth the $25ish I paid for it, but a lot of people trying to make Back 4 Blood content received it for free and at the time it looked fun and I was convinced it would be the next LFD style game for about a week. I was rarely able to queue when I actually got into the game, likely because the max player count probably never exceeded a couple thousand. When I did queue, the game itself was so bare bones that it was nearly impossible to get teammates who could figure out what was going on. There was no massive blinking light to indicate to the smallbrained amongst us where to walk without dying. I gave up and forgot about this game after 4 hours of attempting to finish more than the very first match I ever played.

Perfectly decent L4D-like. A shame more people aren't playing it. I checked the charts and sure enough there were a couple of active players online. We had fun. Very easy to get into, just jumped right into their campaign with no hassle. Game looked and ran well on my rtx 2070s. Persuade your friends to buy it and you are certain to have fun if you enjoy L4D or coop shooters in general.

The game is mid. It's like Left 4 Dead but with a much lower budget and weapons that feel completely unimpactful, both in terms of how they sound and weapon impact. I'm typically lenient with games like this, no matter how clunky they are, because I like supporting indie developers, however I have recently discovered that the lead dev (Chet Faliszek) is a pissbaby who ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and whines about leftists on Bluesky for daring to criticize the Democratic Party and spent a year covering up their involvement in the genocide in Gaza, so I have run out of good will.

This is a review made with bitterness, yes, but it is also honest. This is a game that you want to enjoy, not a game that you actually enjoy. I bought this game a year ago, played it for an hour and a half, and was unimpressed, but decided to wait and see if its issues got fixed. I even convinced a friend to play it with me despite reservations, although it ended up falling to the wayside in favor of playing other, far more enjoyable games. Sadly, I think we are well outside of the refund window.

It is unfortunate for Chet that he cannot simply block reviews to hide them from people, as he likes to do with replies on Bluesky.

The Anacrusis is a fun 4 player co-op that honestly helped me out with my career in making custom maps & level design in general! This was one of my first ways of going into Unreal Engine and learning the tools, doing some awesome level design, and even making my own maps for The Anacrusis. There's a ton of new custom maps that are amazing, and the art-style of the environments are amazing, and all around the gameplay spaces that were designed are pretty freaking awesome.

The Stray Bombay community is a great place to hang out as well! It's active, and there's a ton of Game Nights going on, and you can join the discord to find other people to play as well! 

All around the gameplay is fun, chaotic, and there's multiple difficulties you can play on to experience even more hordes and terror from the aliens. The perk system also offers variety in your play style so you can be a healing grenadier, or a blasting Anacrusis crew mate (which is my favorite style with the Blaster)

The Anacrusis, a game that got lost somewhere somehow. It has the bones of a great L4D style game. Just no meat or any other additions. I don't recommend the game at full price. However the game frequently goes on sale and its mostly 5$ and below. It's fun for the 4 ish hours you'll get from the "story".

 It's quite interesting to see a game like The Anacrusis. Me and my partner were the only 2 people in the world playing this game yesterday. It made the game feel unique. Like you were exploring a lost relic. It's clear The Anacrusis
 was meant to be something more. You can see that in bits of the story and the dialogue. 

The Anacrusis is truly a one of a kind game. It's a bittersweet treat to see a game that had the potential and didn't quite hit the mark.

This game is not horrible, but it is not worth full price.  The basic gun mechanics are fairly good, but the enemies really ruin this game.  Common enemies make 0 noise so you sometimes will turn around with a horde on you from nowhere, and the special enemies are very annoying (the Flasher makes the game lag and everything either too bright or dark).  Overall, if this game is on sale for $1-2 or bundled again it is probably worth getting, but do not get for full price or expect anything similar to Left 4 Dead or anything.

I'd only recommend this game if you get it in a sale or bundle. While the shooting was enjoyable, there just wasn't enough to hook me in. The levels seemed to blend together and there wasn't anything standout like a boss. On top of that, several of the game decisions were just baffling to me.

1. Enemies barely make any noise on their own, and you have to rely on other audio cues for hordes (which sometimes don't work)

2. The "Flasher" enemy that forces you to look at something uncomfortably bright in order to kill it.

3. Odd dialogue that sounds like pieces were recorded in isolation and stitched together.

It definitely wasn't bad, but I have no desire to play it again after beating the episodes.
